Directly standardised rates

Source: R/rates.R
dastd.Rd

The rate each group would have with the stratum make-up (age bands, say) of a standard population: the sum over strata of the standard's weights times the group's stratum rates. The interval is Fay and Feuer's gamma interval; the ratio of two standardised rates has a log-normal interval and their difference a normal one.

Usage

dastd(x, n, strat, grp = NULL, std, ref = NULL, per = 1, level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

The events: numbers from 0; or a clpre list from clprep().

n

The exposure of each row: positive numbers.

strat

The stratum of each row: labels.

grp

NULL (one group) or the group of each row: labels. Each group has one row per stratum.

std

The standard population (or weights) of each stratum: numbers from 0 with a positive sum, named by stratum or in the order of the strata (a factor's levels, or the sorted labels).

ref

The reference group: a label or a position; the first group by default.

per

The rates and differences are given per per units of n (1e5 for rates per 100,000, 100 for percentages): one positive number.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class dastd, a list: rates (group, x the events, rate, lo, hi, var the variance of the rate), cmp (one row per group but the reference: group, ratio, lo, hi, diff, dlo, dhi), ref, per and level.

References

Fay, M. P. and Feuer, E. J. (1997). Confidence intervals for directly standardized rates: a method based on the gamma distribution. Statistics in Medicine, 16(7), 791-801. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19970415)16:7<791::AID-SIM500>3.0.CO;2-#

Examples

d <- data.frame(age = rep(c("18-29", "30-49", "50+"), 2),
                grp = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
                x = c(30, 22, 5, 41, 30, 12),
                n = c(5000, 9000, 6000, 3000, 8000, 7000))
dastd(d$x, d$n, d$age, d$grp, std = c(30, 45, 25), per = 1e4)
#> dastd: standardised rates per 10000
#>  group  x     rate       lo       hi      var
#>      A 57 31.08333 23.49743 40.39982 17.16806
#>      B 83 62.16071 48.83268 78.21030 52.02280
#> against A:
#>  group    ratio       lo      hi     diff     dlo      dhi
#>      B 1.999809 1.414352 2.82761 31.07738 14.7742 47.38057
